JUDGMENT
This claim petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioner is as follows:-
That on 15-07-2024 at about 3-00 p.m. the petitioner was driving Mahindra XUV vehicle bearing No.KA-01-MZ-1122 in which Mr. Settivari Shiva Rama Krishna was travelling and when they reached near Channasandra RNSIT Bridge Nice Road,
Kengeri Bengaluru, at that time the driver of Scorpio vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-MQ-2629 came in a rash and negligent manner, without observing the other vehicular movement and hit to the road divider and came towards opposite lane and dashed to the Mahindra XUV vehicle, result of which the petitioner sustained simple injury on his chest.
Immediately, the petitioner was shifted to Criya Hospital, Kothanoor Village, Bangalore wherein admitted as an inpatient for two days.
So far, the petitioner has spent Rs.23,289/- towards medical expenses.
3. Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy.
He was working as a driver in Briyas Food Pvt Ltd., and earning monthly income of Rs.28,000/- per month.
Due to the permanent disability, he is not in a position to do the said work.
He has suffered pain and sufferings, permanent disability & loss of income.

4. The respondent no.1/the Insurer of Scorpio vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-MQ-2629 has filed written statement and admitted the coverage of insurance policy and the liability if any subject to the terms and conditions mentioned in the policy.
The respondent no.1 has contended that the petitioner has not suffered any permanent disability in the accident.
5. In spite of service of notice, the respondent No.2 - the R.C. owner of Scorpio vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-MQ-2629 has remained absent.
Hence he was placed ex-parte.

6. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues are framed:

sentences.text:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that he had sustained grievous injuries on account of Road Traffic Accident on 15- 07-2024 at about 3-00 pm., near Channasandra, RNSIR Bridge, Nice road, Kengeri, Bangalore, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Scorpio vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-MQ-2629 ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
3. What Order or Award?
7.
The petitioner got examined himself as Pw1 and and got marked documents as Ex.P1 to Ex.P17.
The petitioner has produced memo with wound certificate and got it marked as Ex.P18.
The respondent no.1 has not adduced any evidence on its behalf.

8. Heard arguments of learned counsel for petitioner and respondent no.1 and perused the entire materials placed on record.
9.

My findings on the above issues are as follows:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly in the affirmative.

Issue No.3: As per final order, for the following;
REASONS 10. Issue No.1 : - In order to explain the actionable negligence of the driver of Scorpio vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-MQ-2629, the P.W.1 has filed his affidavit explaining the vivid picture of the accident that took place on 15-07-2024 at about 3-00 p.m. when the petitioner was driving Mahindra XUV vehicle bearing No.KA-01-MZ-1122 (herein after called the offending vehicle) in which Mr. Settivari Shiva Rama Krishna was travelling and when they reached near Channasandra RNSIT Bridge Nice Road, Kengeri Bengaluru, at that time the driver of Scorpio vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-MQ- 2629 came in a rash and negligent manner, without observing the other vehicular movement and hit to the road divider and came towards opposite lane and dashed to the Mahindra XUV vehicle, result of which the petitioner sustained simple injury on his chest 11.

P.W.1 further deposed about the nature of injuries sustained, treatment taken and the amount spent for treatment etc.
12.

In support of the claim and to prove the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle, the P.W.1 has relied upon Ex.P1 to 7 which are the police records such as FIR with complaint, Spot mahazar, sketch, IMV report, charge sheet, Insurance policy of Scorpio vehicle, RC, etc.,
13.

On the basis of the complaint lodged by K T Ankaraju, case has been registered against the driver of offending vehicle in Crime No.0121/2024 of Kengeri Traffic Police Station, for the offence punishable under section 281, 125(a), 106 of BNS 2023.

The investigation officer after investigation Prasanna vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 3 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32893054/
3 filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offence punishable under section 281, 125(b), 106, 125(b) of BNS 2023 and U/Sec. 185 of IMV Act.

sentences.text: 14. So far as the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is concerned, if the spot mahazar and sketch is perused, the offending was proceeding from Sompura-Hosakere Tollgate and the vehicle of the petitioner was proceeding from Hosakere towards Sompura.
There is divider in between the two roads.
The offending vehicle by crossing the road divider entered another lane and hit to the vehicle of the petitioner, which was proceeding in the said lane.

Hence, the very topography of the scene of occurrence would itself sufficient to hold that the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is the sole cause for the accident in which the petitioner has played no role.
Hence, without discussing much on this point, this Court holds issue No.1 in the affirmative.
15. Issue No.2:- The petitioner has given evidence to the effect of his sustained grievous injuries.
As observed earlier, petitioner has produced medical documents i.e., Discharge summary which is at Ex.P11.
On going through the medical documents, it reveals that petitioner has taken treatment at CRIYA Hospital on 15- 07-2024 to 16-07-2024 for a period of one day.
The petitioner has produced wound certificate at Ex.P18.
As per the wound certificate the petitioner has sustained three injuries of which injury No.1 is grievous in nature.
16. The petitioner has not examined the medical officer who has given treatment to him and there is no evidence on record to say that petitioner has suffered permanent disability.
As such there is no loss of future income.
Hence, petitioner is not entitled for compensation under the head of loss of future income.
17. Towards pain and sufferings, the petitioner shown to have sustained three injuries of which one is grievous in nature.

Hence taking in to consideration the nature of injury sustained by the petitioner, time taken for treatment and sufferings during the treatment it is reasonable to hold that petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.60,000/- towards pain and suffering.

18. So far as the medical expenses incurred by the petitioner is concerned, he has produced Inpatient bill issued from CRIYA Hospital for sum of Rs.9,600/- at Ex.P.12 and Medical bills for sum of Rs.13,689/-.
Hence, petitioner is entitled for Rs.23,289/- under the head medical expenses.
19. It is stated that petitioner was aged about 40 years.
He was driver in Briyas Food Pvt., Ltd., and earning Rs.28,000/- p.m..

The petitioner has produced Emplyee ID, pay slips as per Ex.P8 and Ex.P10.
20.

Hence this court considering the age of petitioner, year of accident and place of residence of the petitioner, taken the income of the petitioner at Rs.16,500/- p.m.
21.
The petitioner has sustained one grievous injury and has taken treatment for one day inpatient at CRIYA Hospital.
Hence the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, which is grievous in nature it is reasonable to hold that period of 2 months as complete laid down period.

Hence taking into consideration the avocation of petitioner and loss of income caused from the said avocation,

sentences.text: this court takes the loss of income during laid down period as Rs.16,500/- p.m. for 2 months.

Hence,
the petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.33,000/- towards loss of income during the laid down period .

22. Further for one day of hospitalization at Criya Hospital, Bangalore and for his taking follow up treatment in the said hospital, requires an attendant, was traveled to hospital for treatment, for follow-ups has incurred traveling expenses, he has taken nourishment and need further nourishment at this age and incurred other incidental expenses therefore all together incidental expenses is assessed at Rs.10,000/-.
23. The petitioner at his age of 40 years has suffered one grievous injury which definitely would cause some amount of discomfort and loss of amenities in life.
Hence, petitioner is entitled for compensation under the head loss of amenities and discomfort to the tune of Rs.60,000/-.

Thus the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
Sl. Heads Amount No.
1. Towards pain and sufferings Rs.60,000/-
2.

Medical expenses Rs.23,289/-
3. Towards incidental expenses Rs.10,000/-
4. Loss of income during laid up Rs.33,000/-
 period 5. Loss of discomfort and amenities Rs.60,000/-

Total Rs.1,86,289/-
Therefore this court holds that petitioner is entitled for Rs.1,86,289/- (Rupees One Lakh Eighty Six Thousand Two Hundred Eighty Nine Only).
24.
As regarding liability is concerned, there is no dispute that offending vehicle was insured with 1st respondent and policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Further the driver of the offending vehicle had driving license to drive the offending vehicle.
But if the charge sheet is perused, the driver of the offending vehicle was charge sheeted even for the offence U/Sec.185 of IMV Act for his driving the vehicle under intoxication mind.

It is argued by the learned counsel for petitioner that there is no evidence to say the quantity of liquor consumed by the driver of offending vehicle so as to say that, he has violated the rules by driving the vehicle under intoxication.
But, if the charge sheet is perused, wherein it is clearly stated that the quantity of alcohol consumed by the driver was 30.643 mg., against 100 ml., of blood.
The drink and drive alcohol limit is a blood alcohol concentration of 0.03% or 30 mg of alcohol per 100 ml of blood.
Driving with a blood alcohol concentration exceeding this limit is illegal and it attracts imprisonment U/sec.185 of the Motor vehicles Act 1988.

In the present case the blood alcohol concentration in the body of the driver of the offending vehicle was 30.643 m.g., which is exceeding the limit, hence only the investigating officer filed charge sheet against the driver even for the offence punishable U/sec.185 of IMV Act.

sentences.text: So far as the liability of paying compensation is concerned, it is true that all the documents pertaining to the offending vehicle was in force as on the date of accident but, as observed supra, the driver under the drunken state of mind drive the vehicle and caused for the accident.

26. In a judgment rendered by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA 6922/2014 (MV-D)
decided on 19-06-2025 between Jyothimani Mary Regina and another V/s The Manager, ICICI Lombard Gen. Ins. Co. ltd., and another.

entities.text: Jyothimani Mary Regina and another V/s The Manager, ICICI Lombard Gen. Ins. Co. ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the said case also all the documents pertaining to the offending vehicle was in force, but at the time of accident the driver of the offending vehicle was under the influence of alcohol.

The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has observed that the driving of vehicle under the influence of alcohol may be violation of an implied contract between insurer and insured, but as far as third party is concerned the insurer cannot dis own its liability to pay the compensation.
Sec.147 and 149 of M.V. Act do not state that on that ground insurer can deny its liability to pay the compensation.

Therefore, under such circumstances the insurer is liable to pay the compensation and it is at liberty to recover the same from the owner of the vehicle, since the owner has handed over the vehicle to a person who was driving the vehicle under the influence of alcohol, contrary to provision of Sec.185 of M.V. Act.
27.
In MFA.No.4090 of 2016 (MV-I) decided on 3- 7-2025 between The Oriental Ins. Co. Ltd., V/s Sri.Pratik Kumar Tripathy and others.

entities.text: Oriental Ins. Co. Ltd., V/s Sri.Pratik Kumar Tripathy and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in the similar set of facts has ordered for pay and recovery.
In the said case the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has referred many number of judgments of different High courts decided recently, wherein also pay and recovery was ordered.

Among them the Hon'ble High Court of Kerala in the case of Mohammed Rashid @ Rashid V/s Girivasan E.K. (MACA NO.616/2018 decided on 30-01-2023 reported in 2023 live law (Kerala) 52 held that, in case of drink and drive the owner of the vehicle is liable to pay the compensation and the insurer shall pay the compensation to the third party and recover the same from the owner of the vehicle.
28.

entities.text: Mohammed Rashid @ Rashid V/s Girivasan E.K. (MACA NO.616/2018
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of the observation made by the Hon'ble High courts of different States including our Hon'ble High court and also considering the fact that at the time of accident the driver was under the influence of alcohol, by fastening liability on the respondent no.1 to pay the compensation, at the first instance with interest at 6% per annum from the date of accident till the date of payment of entire amount liberty is given to recover the same from the respondent no.2.
Accordingly, I have answered Issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.
29. Issue No.3:- In the light of findings given on Issue No. 1 and 2, my finding on this Issue is as per the following final order.
ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioner is hereby allowed in part with costs.

The petitioner is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.1,86,289/- (Rupees One Lakh Eighty Six Thousand Two Hundred Eighty Nine Only) with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
